description: For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we are building "RelicOrbit 3D" — an interactive web application designed to tell the stories of NASA's discarded equipment, landers, and rovers left on the Moon and Mars. Using modern Bento Grid UI design, Three.js 3D animations, and an embedded AI tutor, we aim to make space science history engaging and accessible for students and space enthusiasts worldwide.
summary: RelicOrbit is an interactive 3D educational experience that explores the stories of human-made space equipment left on the Moon and Mars. Through a virtual museum, visitors can discover historic missions and explore objects such as Apollo lunar hardware, the Viking 1 lander, and Mars exploration rovers. The project aims to make space exploration history more engaging and accessible by combining immersive 3D presentation with educational storytelling. It highlights the legacy of humanity's exploration beyond Earth and encourages visitors to learn about the technology and missions that helped us explore other worlds.
details:
RelicOrbit is an interactive 3D educational experience that presents the history of human-made space equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It introduces visitors to historic space exploration hardware, including Apollo lunar equipment, Viking 1, and Mars exploration rovers.

The experience uses an interactive virtual museum to make space exploration history easier to explore and understand. Visitors can discover the stories behind these objects and learn about the missions that carried them beyond Earth.

The project was developed using web technologies, including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js-based 3D visualization. Its visual design combines a dark space-inspired environment with cyan highlights to create an engaging educational experience.

RelicOrbit aims to preserve the stories of space exploration equipment and encourage interest in planetary science, engineering, and the history of space exploration.
